introduction: On this Sunday, Sirach teaches that God has set before us fire and water, life and death, and we are free to choose. In the Gospel, Jesus says he has come not to abolish the law but to fulfill it, and he goes to the heart of the commandments: anger, lust and dishonesty. Paul speaks of the hidden wisdom of God, revealed by the Spirit. Let us choose life and follow Christ with our whole heart.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, blessed are those who walk in the law of the Lord. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may teach the law of God as Christ fulfilled it, with truth and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are divided by anger or resentment: that they may be reconciled before bringing their gifts to the altar. Let us pray to the Lord.
For married couples: that they may be faithful in heart as well as in deed. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who face hard moral choices: that they may choose life. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that our yes may mean yes and our no mean no. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you have set before us life and death. Give us the wisdom to choose your ways, and write your law on our hearts. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Not to abolish but to fulfill
reflection.body:
Sirach reminds us that we are free: "If you choose, you can keep the commandments." God "has set fire and water before you. You will stretch forth your hand to whichever you desire. Before man is life and death." God does not force us. He invites us to choose life. And he adds: "He has not given any man license to sin."

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks about the law of Moses. Some thought he had come to set it aside. He says the opposite: "Don't think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn't come to destroy, but to fulfill." And he sets a high standard: "unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven."

Then Jesus shows what this greater righteousness means. Several times he says, "You have heard that it was said... but I tell you." The law says, do not murder; Jesus goes to the root, anger and contempt. The law says, do not commit adultery; Jesus goes to the root, lust in the heart. The law regulates oaths; Jesus asks for simple honesty: let your yes be yes and your no be no.

Jesus is not making the law harder for its own sake. He is showing that God wants our hearts, not just our outward behavior. He gives a striking example: if you are bringing your gift to the altar and remember that your brother has something against you, "leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift." Worship and reconciliation belong together.

Paul says this wisdom comes from God's Spirit: "Things which an eye didn't see, and an ear didn't hear... these God has prepared for those who love him."

This week, look at the roots: anger, resentment, impure thoughts, half-truths. Bring them to God. And if someone has something against you, take a step toward reconciliation.
